                  Audit Question 7.7

 NRC Audit on SMR-300 LWA/CPA Part 1 – Question No. 7.7                 [Receipt Date: 05/11/2026]


       As discussed in SECY 95-132, the purposes of the reliability assurance program for
       passive designs are to provide reasonable assurance that: (1) an advanced reactor is
       designed, constructed, and operated in a manner that is consistent with the assumptions
       and risk insights for these risk significant SSCs, (2) the risk-significant SSCs do not
       degrade to an unacceptable level during plant operations, (3) the frequency of transients
       that challenge advanced reactor SSCs are minimized, and (4) these SSCs function
       reliably when challenged. The NRC staff reviewed the applicant’s Design Reliability
       Assurance Program described in Chapter 17.4 of LWA application. Since the PRA and
       the Safety Analysis are not within the scope of this LWA, the staff can only make a
       regulatory finding on the Design Reliability Assurance program (DRAP) scope (Section
       17.4.1), programmatic controls (Section 17.4.2), methodology including Figure 17.4-1
       (Section 17.4.3), expert panel description (Section 17.4.4), and the process for
       determining dominant failure modes (Section 17.4.6). In this context, the staff reviewed,
       Section 17.4.5, Systems, Structures, and Components within the Scope of the Reliability
       Assurance Program. This section states: “All SSCs listed in Table 3.2-3 will be evaluated
       as potential D-RAP candidates as part of a future licensing application.” Table 3.2-3
       reports the Classification of SMR-300 SSCs for Pioneer Units 1 and 2 LWA. Without the
       PRA and the Safety analysis, the staff cannot conclude that this table is an exhaustive
       list of SSCs that will be scoped into DRAP in future licensing applications.

       The staff is requesting the LWA application be updated to state that (1) the final list of
       DRAP SSCs will be updated pending the results of the DRAP process following
       completion of the PRA and the Safety Analysis and (2) these DRAP results will be
       documented in Table 3.2-3 and Table 17.4-1 consistent with LWA Figure 17.4-1.




SMR Response                                                         [Response Date: 06/8/2026]


The intent of PSAR Section 17.4 is to describe how the D-RAP process is being established and
implemented. As stated in Paragraph 17.4.5, the outcome of the D-RAP process is the
compilation of a list of risk-significant SSCs, referred to as the D-RAP list. The D-RAP list is
being developed by assessing the SSC designs, PSA results, considerations of defense-in-
depth strategies, and relevant operational experience, as they become available. As the
Pioneer Units 1 and 2 project progresses through the final design, construction, commissioning
and operational phases, the D-RAP list will continue to be updated under established
procedures applicable to D-RAP.
Therefore, the list of D-RAP SSCs is maintained as a living document, and will be made
available upon request, along with the applicable D-RAP program documents, procedures and
records, for NRC audits and inspections as part of NRC’s review of the LWA, CP, and OL
applications. Any clarifications or changes to the D-RAP process itself will be documented in a
future revision to the PSAR/FSAR Section 17.4. Holtec is currently revising PSAR Section 17.4
as stated in our responses to NRC’s LWA Audit questions 7.1 – 7.6. We are making one
additional change involving Figure 17.4-1 to improve clarity and consistency as shown below.
        Specifically, the box labeled as "Table 17.4" at the lower right corner is being removed , since
       'Table 17.4" is not referenced anywhere in the PSAR as such a table was not intended to be
       included in the PSAR/FSAR, but rather to be maintained under Holtec's administrative controls.

        Preliminary Analysis and Evaluation Results for Steel-Concrete Containment and
        other SC-I structures
        Regulatory Basis:
        The regulations in 10 CFR 50.10(d)(3(i)) require that an application for an LWA include
        design and construction information otherwise required by the Commission’s rules and
        regulations to be submitted for a construction permit but limited to those portions of the
        facility that are within the scope of the LWA.
        The regulations in 10 CFR 50.34(a)(4) require that the PSAR provide information
        regarding a preliminary analysis and evaluation of the design and performance of
        structures, systems and components (SSCs) (including SC-I structures) of the facility
        with objective of assessing risk to the public and including determination of the margins
        of safety during normal operations and transient conditions, and the adequacy of SSCs
        (including SC-I structures) provided for the prevention of accidents and the mitigation of
        the consequences of accidents.
        Issue:
        The LWA PSAR does not provide the preliminary analysis results and evaluation
        information (evaluating part of the descriptive preliminary design and design bases
        implementation) required by 10 CFR 50.34(a)(4) for the safety-related SC-I Steel-
        Concrete Containment [[
                                    ]]* described in PSAR Section 3.8.1. Further, this
        information is also not provided for other safety-related SC-I structures within the scope
        of the LWA in PSAR Sections 3.8.3 through 3.8.5. The staff needs this information to
        assess safety margins and adequacy of preliminary design implementation of these
        SC-I structures and for a reasonable assurance determination of no significant risk to
        public health and safety.
        Request:
        (1) Provide the preliminary analysis results and evaluation information required by 10
            CFR 50.34(a)(4) for the SC-I Steel-Concrete Containment (SCCV, TG, and basemat)
            within the scope of the LWA described in PSAR Section 3.8.1.

        (2) Provide the preliminary analysis results and evaluation information required by 10
            CFR 50.34(a)(4) for a sample (based on safety-significance) of the SC-I structures
            within the scope of the LWA described in PSAR Sections 3.8.3 through 3.8.5.

        (3) Update the PSAR as needed.

 SMR Response                                                         [Response Date: 07/20/2026]
During the pre-application engagement meetings for the Limited Work Authorization (LWA), Holtec
and the NRC discussed the intended scope and level of detail for the LWA Preliminary Safety
Analysis Report (PSAR). Consistent with those discussions, the LWA PSAR was developed to
provide the preliminary design information necessary to support the limited work activities within
the scope of the LWA, while the detailed structural analyses, complete design evaluations, and
final design verification were planned for inclusion in the subsequent Final Safety Analysis Report
(FSAR).
Holtec understands that the staff is requesting additional preliminary analysis and evaluation
information to support its review under 10 CFR 50.34(a)(4) and to facilitate an independent
assessment of the adequacy of the preliminary structural design and associated safety margins
for the SC-I structures included within the scope of the LWA.
Holtec agrees that providing preliminary analysis results will facilitate the NRC staff's review. At
this time, Holtec does not anticipate the need to revise the LWA PSAR but will provide the below
documents for Staff’s review and understanding as a part of the request.
   1. HI-2251265 – Structural Analysis of the SMR-300 Below-Grade Containment for Design
      Basis Accident Conditions
   2. HI-2240567 – Combined Containment Structure and Reactor Auxiliary Building – South
      Basemat Structural Analysis
   3. HI-2251502 – Combined CS and RAB-South Basemat CSSM Structural Analysis

      Regulatory Basis:
      The regulations in10 CFR 50.34(a)(3)(ii) require that applicants for a construction permit
      (CP) address in the preliminary safety analysis report (PSAR) the design bases and the
      relation of the design bases to the principal design criteria. NUREG-0800, Section 3.8.1
      provides guidance for the review of Concrete Containment which the staff also uses for
      review of Steel-Concrete Containment, as applicable.
      The guidance for CP applications in Appendix A to DNRL-ISG-2022-01 (ADAMS
      Accession No. ML22189A097) states that the applicant for a CP should commit to
      the latest revision of Regulatory Guide (RG) 1.136 (which endorses ASME Section III-
      2, which is applicable to SMR300 SC containment design) or justify an
      alternative approach.

      Issue:
      PSAR Section 3.8.1.3 discusses loads and load combinations for Steel-Concrete
      Containment yet does not reference the SMR-300 Concrete Strengthened Steel
      Structured Design and Analysis Methodology Licensing Topical Report (“CSS Structures
      LTR”) nor RG 1.136, both of which are applicable. Additionally, there are other
      subsections of PSAR Section 3.8.1 to which RG 1.136 may be applicable (e.g., PSAR
      Section 3.8.1.4, Design and Analysis Procedures). PSAR Section 3.8.1.3 also does not
      address:
        i.       creep and shrinkage of concrete used for the Steel Concrete Containment Vessel
                 (SCCV) as recommended in NUREG-0800 acceptance criteria 3.8.1.II.4.D;

        ii.      consideration of dynamic lateral soil pressures on embedded walls of SCCV as
                 recommended in NUREG-0800 acceptance criteria 3.8.1.II.4.E; and

       iii.      effects of vapor pressure from evaporation of moisture from concrete infill of
                 the SCCV under elevated temperatures from design-basis accident conditions.



      Request:


              1. Include a reference to RG 1.136 in applicable subsections (including subsection
                 3.8.1.3) of PSAR Section 3.8.1 where the provisions will be modified or
                 supplemented by RG 1.136, as applicable, or reference the CSS Structures LTR
                 where such modification or supplementation is indicated. Since this design
                 feature is unique to SMR-300, explain how the load due to fluid (water) in the
                 Annular Reservoir (AR) is considered in the design load combinations.
           2. In PSAR Section 3.8.1.4 which describes the design and analysis procedures
             for Steel-Concrete containment, explain how the ultimate internal pressure
             capacity of containment will be determined as a measure of safety margin above
             design basis accident pressure to satisfy GDC 50.

          3. In PSAR Section 3.8.1.4 or in the CSS Structures LTR (with cross-reference to
             the LWA PSAR), describe the methods used for considering creep and shrinkage
             of concrete infill used in the SCCV for composite action.

          4. In appropriate subsection(s) of PSAR Section 3.8.1, describe the methods to
             evaluate effects of vapor pressure for Concrete-Strengthened Steel Module
             (CSSM) structural elements from evaporation of moisture from concrete infill of
             the SCCV under elevated temperatures from design-basis accident conditions,
             and/or provision of measures (e.g., vent holes) to relieve such vapor pressure.

          5. In the appropriate subsection(s) of PSAR Section 3.8, describe the methods used
             for consideration of dynamic lateral soil pressures on the embedded walls of the
             SCCV.



SMR Response R1                                                                 [Response Date: 09/09/2026]
  1. The Annular Reservoir (AR) is formed in the annulus between the above-grade Steel
     Containment Vessel (SCV) and the Containment Enclosure Structure (CES), with the SCV
     forming the inner boundary and the CES forming the outer boundary (PSAR Section
     3.8.1.1.1). The AR-induced load on the TG is treated as a component of the Dead Load
     (D) term in Table 3.8-1, rather than as a separate load symbol, as it is a permanent plant
     feature rather than a transient loading.

      PSAR Section 3.8.1.3 is revised to reflect the same, and a markup is provided to NRC for
      review below.
